title: At school and university
subtitle: study, take an exam, pass, fail
summary: Name school subjects and classroom things, and use the verbs we need to talk about studying and exams.

lesson.heading: School subjects
rows: how things move and work, e.g. E = mc2
what things are made of, e.g. H2O

lesson.heading: Useful things in the classroom
rows: the teacher writes on it with a board pen
it takes the writing off the board
you put notices on it with a drawing pin

machines the teacher uses in class

lesson.heading: School or university?
lesson.text: Children **go to school**; older people **go to university**. A maths teacher **teaches** maths and her students **study** maths. At school, children **learn** to read and write.

examples.text: Children **go to school** at five in Britain.
My sister **goes to university** in Cambridge.
At school children **learn** to read and write.

lesson.heading: Courses, exams and degrees
lesson.text: Students can **do a course** in many schools and universities. At the end of a course you often **take** or **do an exam**. You hope to **pass** your exams; you don't want to **fail** them. If you pass your final exams at university, you **get a degree**.

examples.text: She wants to **do an English course** this summer.

examples.note: You can also say do our exams.

examples.text: He studied hard and **passed** all his exams.
If you **fail** an exam, you can take it again.
Next year she will **get her degree** and look for a job.

lesson.text: Students **do** their homework - not ~~make homework~~ and not ~~homeworks~~. Homework has no plural.

exercises.prompt: Match the subject with what you study in it.
In which subject do you study computers?
In which subject do you do sport?
You use a ___ to take away pencil marks.
exercises.explanation: A rubber takes pencil writing off the paper.

exercises.prompt: You use a ___ to draw a straight line.
exercises.explanation: A ruler is long and flat, and you draw straight lines with it.

exercises.prompt: Put each classroom thing in the right group.
Ethan does well at school. He finds it easy to ___ new things.
exercises.explanation: The teacher teaches and the student learns.

exercises.prompt: He always ___ his homework in the evening.
exercises.explanation: We do homework - not make homework.

exercises.prompt: Ethan is a good student. He usually ___ all his exams.
exercises.explanation: pass an exam = do well in it.

exercises.prompt: If he ___ his exams, he will be very sad.
exercises.explanation: fail an exam is the opposite of pass an exam.

exercises.prompt: Ethan really wants to ___ geography at university.
exercises.explanation: Students study a subject at university.

exercises.prompt: Next year his sister will ___ her degree and then look for a job.
exercises.explanation: You get a degree when you pass your final exams at university.

exercises.statement: After school, students make their homeworks.
exercises.explanation: After school, students do their homework. We do homework, and the word has no plural.

exercises.statement: Children go to school and students go to university.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Note that we say go to school and go to university, with no the.

exercises.prompt: Say what you hope about your exams.
exercises.answer: I hope to pass my exams.
exercises.explanation: You hope to pass, and you don't want to fail.

exercises.prompt: Say when students take an exam.
words: At the end of a course
exercises.answer: At the end of a course you often take an exam.
alternatives: At the end of a course you often take an exam
exercises.explanation: We take or do an exam at the end of a course.
